bugs.title: Unknown loopback peers share one enrollment lock bucket
bugs.summary: When the socket is loopback and the request has no tailnet X-Forwarded-For and no Tailscale-User-Login, the bucket is loopback. Ten failures lock every other unidentified loopback client. A loopback client can also set X-Forwarded-For to another peer's tailnet address and lock that peer when whois names it. Headers from a non-loopback socket are ignored.
bugs.expected: An unidentified client cannot lock an identified tailnet peer, and identified peers do not share the fallback bucket.
bugs.actual: Identified peers stay unlocked when the fallback bucket locks. A loopback spoofed X-Forwarded-For locked tsnode:nIMAC while tsnode:nEVIL still enrolled. A non-loopback X-Forwarded-For was ignored.
repro: Create a node manager with a fake whois
Send ten bad enrollments from 127.0.0.1 with no Tailscale headers
Repeat from ::1 and expect E_IP_LOCKED
Enroll from 127.0.0.1 with X-Forwarded-For of a known tailnet address and expect pending
From loopback, set X-Forwarded-For to a victim tailnet address and send ten failures

history.note: whois was injected. The real tailscale binary was not run. Owner approval is not set.
